---
title: Upload from the browser
description: Add a drop zone that sends a file straight to storage in resumable parts, with your backend deciding who may upload.
---

`<clipmux-uploader>` is a drop zone with a file button, a progress bar,
Cancel and Retry. It asks your backend to create the upload, sends the file
in parts straight to storage (not through your server), resumes after a
dropped connection or a reload, and tells you when the upload is complete.
The browser never holds an API key.

It comes from `@clipmux/uploader`, which has no dependencies.

## Before you start

- A backend route that creates uploads. With `@clipmux/node`, that is the
  `upload` callback of `clipmuxHandler` from the
  [quickstart](/docs/build/quickstart); to write your own, see
  [Your backend route](#your-backend-route) below.
- The package:

<Tabs items={['npm', 'pnpm']}>
<Tab value="npm">

```bash
npm i @clipmux/uploader
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="pnpm">

```bash
pnpm add @clipmux/uploader
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Add the element

```html
<script type="module">
  import '@clipmux/uploader/element'
</script>
<clipmux-uploader create-url="/api/clipmux/upload?lesson=42" accept="video/*" max-size="5000000000"></clipmux-uploader>
```

```ts
const uploader = document.querySelector('clipmux-uploader')!
uploader.addEventListener('clipmux-uploaded', (e) => {
  console.log(e.detail.asset.id) // processing: your webhook hears when it's ready
})
```

When someone chooses or drops a file, the element POSTs
`{"size", "name", "type"}` as JSON to `create-url`, with the page's cookies,
so your backend can check who is asking. Put your own IDs in the URL, as
`?lesson=42` does here.

### Attributes

| Attribute | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `create-url` | Your backend's route that creates the upload. Required. |
| `accept` | The files it takes, as on `<input type=file>`, for example `video/*,.mkv`. Dropped files are checked too. |
| `max-size` | The largest file, in bytes. A larger one fails with `file_too_large` before anything is sent. |
| `state` | Set by the element, for styling: `idle`, `uploading`, `done` or `error`. |

The element also has a few properties and methods:

- `options` takes further upload options: `concurrency` (parts in flight,
  default 4), `maxAttempts` (tries per request, default 6), and `store`
  (where an unfinished upload is remembered, `localStorage` by default;
  `null` turns that off).
- `upload(file)` uploads a file as choosing it does; `retry()` tries the
  last failed upload again; `cancel()` stops it for good and tells ClipMux.
- `state`, `file` and `asset` read the current state, the file and, once
  complete, the video.

### Events

Each event bubbles and is typed.

| Event | `detail` |
| --- | --- |
| `clipmux-progress` | `{ bytesUploaded, bytesTotal, partsDone, partsTotal }` |
| `clipmux-uploaded` | `{ asset }`: the video, now `processing`. |
| `clipmux-error` | `{ code, message, status, error }` |

`clipmux-error`'s `code` is one of:

- `file_type_rejected`: the file doesn't match `accept`.
- `file_too_large`: the file is over `max-size`.
- `create_denied`: `create-url` answered `401` or `403`, for example because
  your `upload` callback returned `null`.
- An error code from ClipMux or storage, such as `too_large` (the file is
  over the server's upload limit), or `network` when the connection kept
  failing.

## Resume and retry

- The file goes in parts of the upload's `part_size` (32 MiB), up to four at
  a time.
- Requests retry by themselves with backoff, honour `Retry-After`, and wait
  while the browser is offline. A `4xx` such as `413 too_large` fails at
  once.
- After a failure, Retry continues from what storage already holds.
- The upload is remembered in `localStorage`, keyed by the file's name,
  size and modification time, until it completes. Choosing the same file
  after a reload, or in a new tab, resumes it. If the remembered upload has
  expired or been cancelled, the element creates a new one.
- An unfinished upload stays resumable for 24 hours. Cancel ends it for
  good: the video becomes `errored` with `upload_cancelled`.

## Style it

- **Parts:** `dropzone`, `label`, `button`, `progress`, `bar`, `status`,
  `cancel` and `retry`.
- **Custom properties:** `--clipmux-uploader-accent`, `--clipmux-uploader-border`,
  `--clipmux-uploader-radius`, `--clipmux-uploader-background`,
  `--clipmux-uploader-color` and `--clipmux-uploader-font`.
- **Slot:** the default slot replaces the drop zone's text, "Drop a video
  here, or".

```css
clipmux-uploader {
  --clipmux-uploader-accent: #0f766e;
  --clipmux-uploader-radius: 4px;
}
clipmux-uploader::part(bar) {
  transition: none;
}
clipmux-uploader[state='error']::part(status) {
  color: #b91c1c;
}
```

```html
<clipmux-uploader create-url="/api/clipmux/upload">Drop your lesson video, or</clipmux-uploader>
```

## React

Import the JSX types once, and load the element in the browser only:

```tsx title="app/lessons/[id]/uploader.tsx"
'use client'
import type {} from '@clipmux/uploader/react' // JSX types only
import { useEffect } from 'react'

export function LessonUploader({ lessonId }: { lessonId: string }) {
  useEffect(() => {
    import('@clipmux/uploader/element')
  }, [])
  return (
    <clipmux-uploader
      create-url={`/api/clipmux/upload?lesson=${lessonId}`}
      accept="video/*"
      onclipmux-uploaded={(e) => console.log(e.detail.asset.id)}
    />
  )
}
```

The types cover the attributes, `options` and the three `onclipmux-…`
events; React itself is not a dependency. React 19 passes the
`onclipmux-…` props to the element as event listeners. On React 18, add the
listeners with a ref and `addEventListener`.

## Your backend route

The element needs `create-url` to answer with the created upload plus
`endpoint`, your ClipMux server's URL. With `clipmuxHandler`, the `upload`
callback returns how to create it, or `null` to refuse:

```ts
async upload(req, { file }) {
  await requireInstructor(req) // your own check
  const lesson = new URL(req.url).searchParams.get('lesson')
  return { passthrough: `lesson_${lesson}`, title: file.name }
}
```

It may also return `playback_policy`, `generate` and `renditions`.

To write the route yourself, check access, call `POST /v1/uploads` with your
API key, and answer with the body. `clipmux.uploads.create` returns it with
`endpoint` already added:

```ts
const upload = await clipmux.uploads.create({ size, passthrough: 'lesson_42' })
return Response.json(upload)
```

Without the SDK, add `endpoint` yourself:

```ts
const res = await fetch(`${process.env.CLIPMUX_URL}/v1/uploads`, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.CLIPMUX_API_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ size, passthrough: 'lesson_42' }),
})
return Response.json({ ...(await res.json()), endpoint: process.env.CLIPMUX_URL })
```

`size` comes from the element's request body. The upload token in the answer
reaches only that one upload.

## Content-Security-Policy

A page with the uploader must allow, besides its own origin:

- `connect-src`: your ClipMux server's URL, and the storage origins the
  parts go to (`upload_origins` from `GET /v1/app`; the server's own URL
  when it stores files on its own disk);
- `style-src 'unsafe-inline'`, for the element's styles.

`npx @clipmux/node doctor` prints the exact origins. Storage must also
expose the `ETag` header to the page; ClipMux sets that up on its own disk
and on the buckets it connects.

## Check it works

Choose a short video. The bar fills, the status reads "Uploaded" and the
`clipmux-uploaded` event fires with a video in `processing`. Then your
webhook receives `video.asset.ready`.

- `create_denied`: your route refused, or the browser sent no session
  cookie. Check `create-url` is on your own origin.
- `create_invalid`: your route answered without an upload. It must return
  the body of `POST /v1/uploads`, with `endpoint`.
- `etag_not_exposed`: storage doesn't expose `ETag` to the page; fix the
  bucket's CORS rules.
- A request blocked in the console: the Content-Security-Policy is missing an
  origin. Run `doctor`.
